entries.mechanism: The 2026 pipeline reports 1335.00 (before credits) and TAXSIM 2024 reports 649.52, a positive 685.48-dollar gap (the pipeline is higher). TAXSIM 2024 applies the 4.55 per cent rate (raising its tax by 30 dollars on 30,000) but then nets the section 59-10-1018 taxpayer tax credit (about 715 dollars at this income) that this before-credits core excludes; the credit dominates. The residual is the rate vintage plus the taxpayer-credit scope, both documented boundaries of this before-credits core.

The 2026 pipeline reports 2670.00 and TAXSIM 2024 reports 2404.52, a 265.48-dollar gap: the 4.55-vs-4.45 rate vintage (+60 dollars in TAXSIM on 60,000) net of the partially-phased-out 59-10-1018 taxpayer credit (about 325 dollars) that this before-credits core excludes.

The 2026 pipeline reports 6675.00 and TAXSIM 2024 reports 6825.00, a clean -150.00-dollar gap: at this income the section 59-10-1018 taxpayer credit is fully phased out, leaving only the 4.55-vs-4.45 rate vintage (150,000 x -0.001 = -150). The residual is exactly the rate vintage.

The 2026 pipeline reports 2670.00 and TAXSIM 2024 reports 1299.05, a 1370.95-dollar gap: the rate vintage (+60 dollars in TAXSIM on 60,000) net of the larger married section 59-10-1018 taxpayer credit (about 1,431 dollars) that this before-credits core excludes.

The 2026 pipeline reports 5340.00 and TAXSIM 2024 reports 4809.05, a 530.95-dollar gap: the rate vintage (+120 dollars in TAXSIM on 120,000) net of the partially-phased-out married taxpayer credit (about 651 dollars) that this before-credits core excludes.

The 2026 pipeline reports 13350.00 and TAXSIM 2024 reports 13650.00, a clean -300.00-dollar gap: the taxpayer credit is fully phased out, leaving only the 4.55-vs-4.45 rate vintage (300,000 x -0.001 = -300).
